Theorem
[Variational characterization of minimizer] ↗ thm:existence-minimizer-obstacle-problem 1. ch8:8.4-thm-4\group Variational Inequalities

Let $u \in \mathcal{A}$ be the unique solution of \[ I[u] = \min _{w \in \mathcal{A}} I[w]. \] Then \[ \int _U Du \cdot D(w - u)\, dx \geq \int _U f(w - u)\, dx \quad \text{for all } w \in \mathcal{A}. \tag {26} \] We call (26) a variational inequality.

Proof

\sketch For a minimizer, test the segment $u+\tau (v-u)$ and take the one-sided derivative at zero. Conversely, convexity bounds $I[v]-I[u]$ below by this first variation, so the variational inequality implies minimality.

□
